exam_structure.paper_name: Rome and its neighbours — Compulsory Longer Period Study
exam_structure.overview: Q1(a)–(c) Discrete factual knowledge (4m, AO1); Q2 Outline historical events/features in continuous prose (6m, AO1); Q3 Unseen ancient passage + own knowledge (10m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO3); Q4 Same unseen passage + own knowledge on second-order concepts (15m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO2 + 5 AO3); Q5 Two-Era Evaluative Essay spanning at least TWO eras (20m + 5 SPaG = 25m: 10 AO1 + 10 AO2 + 5 SPaG).

consistentThemes: Impact of warfare and military change

sections.title: Key Time Span 1: The legendary kings: Origins of Rome, 753–616 BC

topics.title: 1.1 Aeneas, Romulus and Archaeological Origins
points: The Aeneas and Romulus foundation myths
The nature and origin of the historical evidence for this period, including archaeological and geographical issues

topics.title: 1.2 Romulus' Institutions, Sabines, Senate and Army
points: Romulus' political initiatives; Rome's relationship with the Sabines; the role of the Senate; Romulus' death
Romulus' religious initiatives
Romulus' organisation of the Roman army; Romulus' conflicts with neighbouring communities

topics.title: 1.3 Numa Pompilius, Tullus Hostilius and Ancus Marcius
points: The succession of Numa; Numa's diplomacy and religious policies; Numa's religious reforms
The legal system in the reign of Tullus Hostilius; Tullus Hostilius' conflict with Alba Longa
Ancus Marcius' expansion of Rome

sections.title: Key Time Span 2: The Etruscan kings, 616–509 BC

topics.title: 2.1 Tarquinius Priscus, Urban Rome and Etruscan Power
points: The manner in which each monarch gained power; the methods adopted by the Etruscan Kings to secure their power
The development of the city of Rome; the importance of the Tarquin's personal wealth in gaining popularity
The political and economic significance of Tarquinius Priscus' victories

topics.title: 2.2 Servius Tullius: Omens, Reforms and Army Reorganisation
points: Servius Tullius' reforms; the influence of omens ascribed to Servius Tullius
Reorganisation of the army; the political and economic significance of Servius Tullius' victories

topics.title: 2.3 Tyranny of Tarquinius Superbus and Evidence for the Etruscan Era
points: The tyranny of Tarquinius Superbus; the impact of Tarquinius Superbus' military record
The nature and origin of the historical evidence for this period, including both the literary and archaeological sources

sections.title: Key Time Span 3: Origins of the Republic, 509–494 BC

topics.title: 3.1 Expulsion of Superbus, Consulship and Senate
points: The removal of Tarquinius Superbus; the creation of the early Republic including the development of the Consulship and the Senate

topics.title: 3.2 Silva Arsia, Lars Porsena and Lake Regillus
points: Military challenges to the early Republic and the Roman response, including the Battle of Silva Arsia, the invasion of Lars Porsena and the Battle of Lake Regillus

topics.title: 3.3 Patrician-Plebeian Tensions and Early Republican Evidence
points: Impact of the foundation of the Republic upon the plebeian and patrician class, in particular the tensions developing between the two groups
The nature and origin of the historical evidence for this period

sections.title: Key Time Span 4: Securing the Republic, 494–440 BC

topics.title: 4.1 Sicinius, First Secession and Plebeian Soldier Leverage
points: The development of Plebeian influence on government; Sicinius and the First Secession of the Plebeians
Change and continuity in patrician and plebeian lives; the power of the patricians relative to the plebeians; problems facing the plebeian class
The military implications of the plebeian revolts and the role of soldiers in those revolts; impact of war upon Roman politics

topics.title: 4.2 Volero Publilius (471 BC) and the Appius Claudius Family
points: The Volero Publilius uprising and the reforms of 471
The impact of Appius Claudius and his family upon patrician and plebeian relations

topics.title: 4.3 Decemvirates, Twelve Tables, Second Secession and Valerio-Horatian Laws
points: The Decemvirates, Second Secession and Twelve Tables
The Valerio-Horatian laws and the other reforms of the 440s
The nature and origin of the historical evidence for this period
